newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HEARTS HAVE FOUR SENT OFF AT RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HEARTS HAVE FOUR SENT OFF AT RANGERS.

text.p: Edinburgh side Hearts had four players sent off as they crashed 3-0 to Glasgow Rangers in the Scottish Premier League on Saturday. Pasquale Bruno, David Weir, Neil Pointon and Paul Ritchie were all dismissed in a chaotic second half at Ibrox for crimes ranging from late tackles to "violent conduct" and "use of foul and abusive language".
The match brought back memories of a notorious Scottish Cup quarter-final between bitter Glasgow rivals Rangers and Celtic in 1991, in which four players were sent off.
The first half was largely uneventful, with Scotland striker Gordon Durie putting Rangers ahead just before the break.
But Hearts' world began to collapse around their heads soon after the restart, when Bruno was sent off for tripping Durie, his second bookable offence.
England midfielder Paul Gascoigne took advantage of the extra man within minutes, shrugging off his marker and rounding Hearts 'keeper Gilles Rousset to score Rangers' second.
Hearts were reduced to nine men when Weir was dismissed by referee Jerry Evans for clashing with Durie.

Pointon was next to go, shown the yellow card for the second time for shouting at the linesman and kicking a goalpost, and Ritchie soon followed him to the changing rooms -- again for disputing a decision with the touch judge.
Rangers scored a third through Ally McCoist in a farcical last quarter of an hour, ensuring the defending champions maintain their 100 percent record with five wins from five.
Celtic, who took a first half lead at Dundee United through Dutchman Pierre Van Hooydonk, had Brian O'Neil sent off but still came away with a 2-1 win after a tense last five minutes.
Gary McSwegan looked to have earned Dundee a point with an 87th minute equaliser, but Malky Mackay scored Celtic's winner in the final seconds.
The excitement was too much to bear for a group of Celtic fans, who smashed the window of the press box, showering reporters with glass.
